overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: councilors attended police listening sessions in groups below a quorum with no deliberation shown, and the president-coaching allegation did not involve quorum communications.

allegations.summary: Councilors allegedly deliberated outside a properly noticed meeting by attending three police listening sessions at the Police Department.
allegations.key_passage: Absent evidence to the contrary, we credit the Council’s version of events and find that the Council did not deliberate outside of a properly noticed meeting.

allegations.summary: Whether a quorum of councilors, across the separate listening sessions or otherwise, deliberated serially or simultaneously before the December 12 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We also find no evidence that a quorum of councilors engaged in any discussion of business within the Council’s jurisdiction—either serially or simultaneously—at the listening sessions or on other occasions prior to the posted December 12 meeting.

allegations.summary: The Council President allegedly coached police officers to make statements at the sessions to sway councilors' votes in her favor.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law
